patch_resolves_note: The fixed loop in mpz_init_set_str() changes the counter to signed int and adds i>=0, so the original 128-digit PoC no longer executes the first digit read when the sign-extended pool length is negative.

root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before mpz_init_set_str() enters the descending digit loop, len >= 0 must hold so the first indexed read only uses digits within the supplied string.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original reaches the digit loop with the sign-extended negative length forwarded from the bigint pool header. The fixed original suppresses the protected read for that case, and the adjacent 127-digit witness executes the same read with a non-negative length.

nodes.state: At the bigint pool header store, buf[0] holds the signed char length byte while plen still names the full digit-string length, so the stored header length no longer equals the actual decimal digit count.
At the first digit read, the wrapped loop index i is already greater than or equal to the actual digit-string length, so s[i] reads outside the supplied decimal buffer.

edges.relation: The signed length byte stored in the bigint pool header is reloaded unchanged by the VM as the len argument to mrb_bint_new_str().
The VM-reloaded bigint length is forwarded unchanged into mrb_bint_new_str().
mrb_bint_new_str() passes the same length value into mpz_init_set_str() at the missing non-negative-length guard site.
The wrapped loop index created when mpz_init_set_str() enters the descending digit loop is the same index consumed by the first s[i] read.
